incoming.explanation: The same memorial that carries the unreliable birth/origin tradition also supplies a separate, uncorroborated burial-place datum worth checking on its own terms.
The Newgate-apprentice reading explains the tradition rather than confirming it, and weighs directly against treating it as data about John's own birth or origin.

outgoing.explanation: Illustrates family memory preserving a real biography attached to the wrong man.

shortLabel: American tradition: John Gurney born 29 Sept 1615, Southwark/"Brent" origin

sources.locator: AccessGenealogy transcription of Representative Men and Old Families of Southeastern Massachusetts (1912): 29 Sept 1615 birth, John as John Newgate's apprentice
vol. 26 (1926), David Allston Gurney/Gurney family entry, pp. 230-255: birth 29 Sept 1615, "probably from Southwark, near London Bridge"
memorial 252975617: birth 29 Sept 1615, "London Borough of Brent, Greater London, England"; death 16 March 1663 Braintree

statement: Three American genealogical sources give John Gurney a birth of 29 September 1615 in England: American Biography (1926), locating him "probably from Southwark, near London Bridge"; the Lysander Franklin Gurney sketch (1912, an earlier printing of the same tradition, framing John as John Newgate's apprentice); and a Find a Grave memorial (no. 252975617), locating the birth in the anachronistic modern place name "London Borough of Brent, Greater London" (Brent was created in 1965 and cannot describe a seventeenth-century parish). All three repeat the identical date across compilations a century apart.
